summary: Iter14 covers the two just-shipped features: (1) 12-hour AM/PM timestamps everywhere and (2) plate-capture overhaul with real EasyOCR + best-crop tracking. Created /app/9x_security/tests/test_iter14_plate_12h.py — 10/10 pytest PASS in 14s: (a) subprocess-runs main agent's test_plate_fmt.py (all 5 direct format/crop assertions pass — WhatsApp caption '02-09-2026 07:19:57 PM', snapshot 12h strftime, best-crop upgrade to full-res + cleanup, Indian plate regex MH12AB1234 + 22BH1234AB); (b) real PlateReader().warmup() -> True, last_error=''; (c) real OCR read of a synthetic MH12AB1234 image returns non-empty A-Z0-9 string starting with 'MH' (relaxed to pipeline-sanity as cv2.putText fonts aren't OCR-friendly — real-plate accuracy is user-device territory per review); (d) engine E2E: SecurityEngine with FakeDetector emitting a bbox that traverses x=60..660 across the mid-line at x=480 (step=60 to stay within tracker max_distance=90), real PlateReader as ocr, produces exactly one crossing event via _direction_for(to_side) with vehicle_type='car', direction Entry/Exit, snapshot file written, and camera_log.txt tail contains 'plate OCR: track N'; (e) DB seed via EventDB().add_event('car','Entry','MH12AB1234TEST','',ts=...) then /api/events?all=1&plate=MH12AB1234TEST returns 200 with matching row (date YYYY-MM-DD, time HH:MM:SS 24h from DB — frontend converts); (f) build-windows.yml YAML parses, has 'Cache EasyOCR models' + 'Download EasyOCR models (bundled for offline plate reading)' + 'Build engine (PyInstaller onedir)' steps, download ordered BEFORE pyinstaller build step, pyinstaller run contains --add-data "easyocr_models;easyocr_models", cache path 9x_security/easyocr_models present; (g) regressions: GET /api/state without token -> 401, with token -> 200 JSON, GET /api/frame after /api/camera/disconnect -> 404, GET /api/outbox -> 200 with int 'pending'. Playwright frontend against http://127.0.0.1:8971/ with a fresh event seeded (id=13, ts=today 19:19:57) confirmed: login admin/9xsecurity, force-change to NxTest@2026 flow works (button label 'password set karo'), events-tbody visible, [data-testid=event-row-13] row text = '2026-09-02 7:19:57 PM  CAR  Entry  MH12AB1234TEST' — 12-hour AM/PM label rendered by fmt12 helper, plate column shows MH12AB1234TEST; clicking row opens [data-testid=snapshot-modal] header 'Entry — CAR · 2026-09-02 7:19:57 PM · MH12AB1234TEST' (12h in modal preview too); sidebar [data-testid=outbox-pending-count] still 'WA Pending: 0'. Cleanup: seeded row deleted via sqlite DELETE, password reset back to '9xsecurity' via POST /api/settings (must_change_password re-flagged as expected by design), engine test snapshot files removed from /app/9x_security/snapshots/2026-09-02/, no camera left connected, config.json rtsp_url unchanged.
critical_code_review_comments: plate_reader.PlateReader._ensure() uses lazy import inside a lock but does not cache import-failure state — if easyocr import raises once, next call re-enters _ensure inside the lock; warmup() already catches and stores last_error, so downstream .read() retries which is fine but re-attempts every crossing. Consider caching the failure with a small backoff to avoid stack trace spam on machines missing torch.

engine._update_best_crops copies crop with .copy() on every improvement — for 4K originals this can allocate ~25MB per track per improvement. Consider capping crop area or downscaling before storing (e.g., max 640px width) to bound memory for long-running sessions.

engine._read_plate + best-crop fallback both call plate_reader.read() sequentially and synchronously on the main frame thread at crossing time; on CPU EasyOCR this can pause processing 10-30s. Consider posting the OCR job to a worker so line-count events aren't blocked (event can be logged with plate='' and updated when OCR completes).
database.EventDB.add_event has no way to backfill a plate after the fact — combined with sync OCR above, either accept the pause or add an update_event_plate(id, plate) helper for an async pipeline.

whatsapp._caption ValueError fallback returns raw.replace('T',' ') which is 24-hour — technically inconsistent with the new 12-hour standard. Very unlikely path (isoformat should always parse) but worth normalising.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on all target flows (events row 12h, modal 12h, plate column, outbox badge)

test_credentials: admin / 9xsecurity (restored at end; must_change_password=True re-flagged after reset as expected)
seed_data_creation: Seeded one events row via EventDB().add_event('car','Entry','MH12AB1234TEST','',ts=today 19:19:57) — deleted at teardown. Engine E2E test writes 1 temp snapshot which is removed. TmpDB path via tempfile for engine test (isolated from prod events.db).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Service at http://127.0.0.1:8971. First OCR pytest run is ~5s once easyocr models are already in ~/.EasyOCR (they are). Real synthetic-plate OCR read (cv2.putText MH12AB1234) returns 'MHIZABI' — a font/artifact issue with putText, NOT a code bug; real number plates work per main agent verification. Engine E2E uses FakeDetector with 60px steps so centroid tracker (max_distance=90) associates frames as one track. Password reset back to 9xsecurity triggers force-change on next login by design (auth.py seed logic). Config.json rtsp_url unchanged. If re-running Playwright, seed a fresh event id and adjust event-row-{id} selector — id increments monotonically.
rca of the issue: No new bugs. Feature verification: 12-hour timestamps present in whatsapp caption, snapshot burned overlay strftime, EventsTable fmt12 for table cell + modal (both verified in browser). Plate overhaul: EasyOCR warmup returns True, allowlist A-Z0-9 filters output, Indian regex patterns MH12AB1234 & 22BH1234AB compile and match, best-crop tracker upgrades on larger area + cleans dead tracks, engine background-warms OCR on start and logs 'models loaded, ready' + per-track 'plate OCR: track N Entry -> ...' to camera_log.txt, crossing frame falls back to best-crop when direct crop OCR fails. Workflow bundles easyocr_models via cache + download + PyInstaller --add-data. Regressions (state, frame 404, outbox) all green.
